VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Checked endpoints (0, 1 and all α_n, β_n). Derivative at endpoints uses one‑sided limits internally, and [0,1] is nondegenerate so every point is a limit point of the domain. All intervals I_n are pairwise disjoint and lie inside (0,1]; the gaps between them are nonempty. No division by zero occurs (h_n > 0, denominators in difference quotients are bounded away from zero on the relevant neighbourhoods). Existential instantiations are finite or from the Archimedean property; no choice principle beyond first‑order logic is used. The unboundedness argument explicitly evaluates G′ at a concrete interior point of each bump. No boundary case breaks the construction.

SOURCES: All 25 declared dependencies and the corresponding cited items were inspected in their complete exact‑current text. Every usage (derivative algebra, chain rule, limit‑point properties, locality of limits, one‑sided limits, the definition of Darboux sums requiring boundedness, Archimedean property and its reciprocal form, order properties, finite‑set minimum, etc.) matches the statement and hypotheses of the cited source.

CHECKED: Title, public claim, every numbered proof step (1.1–9.1), and the Remarks were reviewed. The constructed G is differentiable on the whole closed interval, its derivative G′ is unbounded, and therefore G′ is not bounded, hence has no Darboux sums and is not Riemann integrable. The argument refutes the false claim without circularity or missing necessary hypotheses. No fatal defect was found.
